finding.claim: Pool-level escape() falls back to backslash escaping even when the server runs with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, because _searchInfo() never finds an active connection's status. A quote in an attacker-controlled value breaks out of the string literal.
finding.source: Application value passed to pool.escape(value) (e.g., a search term or username from an HTTP request). pool-promise.js:61-62 and pool-callback.js:63-64 expose this publicly.
finding.sink: SQL string the application builds from pool.escape() output, e.g. WHERE name = ${pool.escape(v)}.

trace.note: _searchInfo takes #idleConnections.get(0); undefined when all connections are busy.
for...in over Object.keys(#activeConnections) iterates index strings '0','1',..., not thread IDs.
#activeConnections['0'] is normally undefined, so the break on line 386 fires and conn stays undefined.
conn falsy, so info stays null and is returned on line 394.
String value goes to escapeString(info, value) with info = null.
Selects CHARS_GLOBAL_REGEXP and LITTERAL_ESCAPE: backslash escaping, so ' becomes \' and \ becomes \\.
Output wrapped in single quotes; under NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES the server treats backslash as literal, so \' closes the literal early.

finding.guards_checked: Idle-connection path (status-based escaping) is not taken when no idle connection exists. No status check, error, or fail-closed behavior when info is null. Connection-level escape (connection.js:113) is correct because it binds live info. escapeId unaffected.

finding.claim: With permitSetMultiParamEntries enabled, object keys are placed into a backtick-quoted identifier without escaping, so a key containing a backtick injects SQL.
finding.source: Object keys from untrusted input, e.g. connection.query('UPDATE t SET ?', obj) where obj is built from a request body.
finding.sink: SET/WHERE clause text sent to the server.

trace.note: Branch taken when opts.permitSetMultiParamEntries is true for a plain object.
for (let key in value): key used as-is.
out += '`' + key + '`=' with no backtick doubling.
Same unescaped pattern on the query-send path: out.writeString('`' + key + '`').

finding.guards_checked: Option is off by default (connection-options.js:132). Values are escaped, but keys are not. No identifier validation or allowlist on this path.

finding.claim: On a non-TLS connection without a configured key, the client requests the server's RSA public key over the unauthenticated channel and encrypts the password with it. An on-path attacker can substitute a key and recover the password.
finding.source: Network-path attacker (MITM) on a plaintext connection to the DB server; the server's key response is trusted without pinning.
finding.sink: Password sent as RSA-OAEP ciphertext under an attacker-supplied key (sha256-password-auth.js:130-137).

trace.note: Branch on opts.ssl; without TLS the key-retrieval path is reached.
A configured cachingRsaPublicKey is used if provided (pinned).
out.writeInt8(0x02) requests the public key from the server.
Server PEM parsed by retrievePublicKey with no fingerprint or signature check.
Password RSA-encrypted with that key and sent.

finding.guards_checked: TLS and cachingRsaPublicKey/rsaPublicKey pinning are the mitigations. No key pinning or fingerprint check by default; matches MySQL protocol design, so may be accepted risk. Touches authentication; flag for Security review.
